questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests precise bit-mmask construction under edge-case shifts; no loops/branches is a common constraint in low-level systems.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masks and ranges
- Safe shifts with variable width (1..32)
- No branching; single expression mask composition

## Code Example
```javascript
uint32_t clearRange32(uint32_t x, unsigned a, unsigned b) {
  unsigned w = b - a + 1; // width of range
  uint32_t ones = (~0u) >> (32 - w); // w ones in LSBs
  uint32_t mask = ~(ones << a); // zeros in [a,b], ones elsewhere
  return x & mask;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to generalize to 64-bit with the same constraints?
- What if inputs are signed; does behavior change in C/C++?

- Bit shifts and masking
- Width awareness and undefined behavior avoidance

uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t n, unsigned r) {

}

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to reason about 128-bit layout, edge cases, and using 64-bit intrinsics for performance.

## Key Concepts
- 128-bit value as hi/lo halves
- Most significant set bit index calculation
- Handling zero input

## Code Example
```c
int highestSetBitIndex128(uint128 x) {
  if (x.hi) return 64 + (63 - __builtin_clzll(x.hi));
  if (x.lo) return (63 - __builtin_clzll(x.lo));
  return -1;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to implement without builtins?
- Extend to 256-bit type?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose bit-fields into a compact word, a common protocol task.

## Key Concepts
- Bit masking
- Bit shifts
- Width enforcement

## Code Example
```javascript
// C-like pseudocode for clarity
uint32_t packHeader(uint8_t version, uint8_t type, uint32_t length) {
  return ((uint32_t)(version & 0xF) << 28) | ((uint32_t)(type & 0xFF) << 20) | (length & 0xFFFFF);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate inputs without branching?
- How would you extend to 64-bit headers with more fields?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement a rotation primitive with wrap-around using only shifts and masks, including masking to handle large r and the n=0 edge case.

## Key Concepts
- Circular shift using (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n))
- Masking r with 31 to confine to 0..31
- Edge-case n=0 preserves x exactly

## Code Example
```c
static inline uint32_t rotl32(uint32_t x, unsigned r) {
  unsigned n = r & 31; // 0..31
  return (x << n) | (x >> (32 - n));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you generalize to 64-bit rotates?
- What are the potential performance differences vs. compiler intrinsics like _rotl?
- How would you test across boundary values (r=0, r=31, r=32, r=33)?
